newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia warns groups to call off E.Timor meeting.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia warns groups to call off E.Timor meeting.

text.p: Malaysia's Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Thursday that human rights groups should call off a planned conference on East Timor or the government would take action.

The national news agency Bernama quoted Anwar as telling reporters the government would take appropriate action under the laws of the country if the organisers refused to cancel the November 9-12 conference.
Some 200 people from 24 countries and 75 organisations were expected to attend the second Asia Pacific Conference on East Timor at a Kuala Lumpur hotel, organisers said.

Malaysia opposes the conference for fear of harming its ties with Indonesia, which invaded East Timor in December 1975 and annexed the Portuguese colony the next year. The United Nations still recognises Lisbon as the administering authority for the territory.

Local journalists said Deputy Home Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayob had asked them at a closed-door meeting on Wednesday not to report on the conference, but said the government would not stop the meeting or keep foreign journalists from covering it.

Immigration authorities had earlier refused to allow a Philippines human rights activist into the country for the conference. Renato Constantino Jr., who had organized the first such conference in Manila in 1994, was stopped by immigration officials at the Kuala Lumpur airport on Wednesday night, conference organisers said.
